    Construction

    Rim routed in two halves from 6/4 Honduran mahogany and glued on dowels, 2.25 in tall for a 2.5 in body: 7 mm walls, 12 × 8 mm glue ledges routed in place of kerfed linings, solid neck and tail blocks, open-top mortise for the set neck's tenon. Every part is cut on a 3-axis router in one or two setups. Spruce top carved as flat planes: a 5 mm hexagonal bridge plateau inside a symmetric eight-sided arch zone, 14 facets in all, with a flat skirt outside it that lands on the rim. A 5 × 6 mm ring beam and two 6 × 9 mm parallel tone bars with scalloped ends run under the plateau's long sides, and a 6 × 7 mm cross bar braces the flat upper bout from the neck block. Top is quartersawn Sitka spruce, dyed black under the shellac, with a quarter-inch undyed band left around the edge as a faux binding. Back is quartersawn bigleaf maple in a shallower faceted arch, glued on, stiff enough to reflect energy back into the top.

    The pickguard never touches the top. It carries the pickup on its tab and is held at two points: a strap screwed into the treble rim, and a 1.5 mm plate under the fingerboard extension, where the guard and the board's underside share one plane.
